hypothesis: Applying BL31's cold-boot security writes at EL3, DCDC4 at 960 mV and the GPU core clocked from PLL_GPU0 at 1008 MHz makes the GPU core identity readable.

conditions.image: diagnostic image applying the three steps

conclusion: The three steps together make the identity readable; the design makes them the default GPU power path.
narrative: A diagnostic image applied three steps that the vendor stack performs and SunstoneOS did not, then read the GPU core identity 36.56.104.183; every earlier image without them stalled at that read. The log records every EL3 write with the word read before and after it. The 22 SPC words at 0x02054004 + 0x10*n and the three R_SPC words read 0 before and after their 0xffffffff writes (write-only set registers, so readback cannot confirm them). SPC 0x020540e0, port 14's status word, changed from 0x1060 to 0xfffffbff (BL31 writes this word directly; port 14's set register is 0x020540e4, which BL31 does not write). PRCM_SEC_SWITCH_REG (0x07010290) and CCMU_SEC_SWITCH_REG (0x02003f00) changed from 0 to 7. DCDC4's selector changed from 0x9e to 0xae (bit 7, set by boot0, kept; 800 mV to 960 mV). PLL_GPU0 locked within four reads each time and read 0xf9105300; both GPU clock update bits cleared on the first read. CORE6 stayed at status 0 for 50 us after its PWCR and policy writes and reached status 8 once the clocks ran, 3,151 us after the observation started. Write 11 (S_TZMA) was not made; the run made writes 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and 17 and returned to the ROM, and the ROM answered. Which of the three steps is necessary is not separated: the manual states the PLL and PRCM security switches have no effect in non-security mode (manual 4.2.5.26) and PLL_NPU has been enabled and locked from non-secure EL1 without the switch, so the switch writes are probably inert; the supply and the GPU PLL remain the candidates.

hypothesis: The power-only diagnostic completes two ON/OFF cycles on the default path.
conclusion: TOP5 OFF closes the GPU master gates; resource acquisition must not require them open while TOP5 is OFF.
narrative: Cycle 1 completed: ON reached CORE6 status 8 (policy_status=0x8, misr_late=0x100) with PLL_GPU0 locked at 1008 MHz; OFF completed all 18 steps and the resource release passed (phase=4 error=0 step=18); snapshot 2 shows TOP5 and CORE6 policy and status 0, GPU clock word and bus gate 0 and PLL_GPU0 0x01105300. This was the first TOP5 transition from ON on a board. Cycle 2's resource acquisition failed (GPU resources result=3 error=7 stage=8 last=0x1101037f, the manager's FAULT with error GATE at its eighth read): CCU 0x5c0 (AHB_MAT_CLK_GATING_REG) bit 7, the GPU0 AHB gate, was clear, a keyed write opened it and the readback was still clear; 0x1101037f is the reset value 0x110103ff without bit 7. TOP5 OFF closed the gate and the gate takes no write while TOP5 is OFF. Cycle 2's controller never started: no PLL_GPU0 enable, no lock or update reads. The vendor's next ON never reads the master gates, so the vendor cannot observe this. The fix leaves the gates alone while TOP5 is OFF, admits a domain-5 ON from OFF with them closed, and requires them open after TOP5 ON. checks/a733-gpu-second-on.c runs both cycles through the real platform, resource manager, controller and owner; built against the tree before the fix (-DBOARD_RUN) it reproduces the board values exactly.

hypothesis: With the gate check moved after TOP5 ON, the power-only diagnostic completes cycle 2.
conclusion: The gate handling was correct; the delay-row writes were removed. Whether TOP5 ON reopens the gates is answered by later firmware-start and firmware-stop images (docs/designs/gpu-firmware-stop.md).
narrative: Cycle 1 ON and OFF passed again; the GPU gates line showed that TOP5 OFF closes both master gates: AHB 0x1101037f and MBUS 0xf1045803 (bit 16 cleared). Cycle 2's acquisition passed with TOP5 OFF (stage=6, its TOP5 status read), the ON relocked PLL_GPU0 (four reads per lock wait) and requested domain 5. The owner then failed the domain, so the controller stopped with phase=5 error=7 step=48: error DOMAIN at the domain-5 request. Failure was at the CORE6 delay row (the controller no longer writes the delay-row words, which no reference writes) and not at the gates.

hypothesis: An OFF and a second ON in one lifetime complete on the default path.
prediction: Each image is one bounded returning run on port 3-1 after a cold DDR start and the frozen provider-readiness checkpoint of the same lifetime, lowest recovery risk first: the power-only diagnostic (bundle row 12, no GPU-window access), then the identity diagnostic (row 13), both two ON/OFF cycles. Set ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/board-bundles-20261025-9/port-3-1/ freezes the lifetime: provider-readiness checkpoint 3adfa4ad... (s11-gpr), power-only b163b8fc... (s11-gpo), identity 01849e62... (s11-gpi), runbook at port-3-1/runbook.md. Both images link 23 objects of the checkpoint and compile 14. Predictions: the monitor makes the security writes and the run returns to a responsive ROM; DCDC4 reads selector 0x9e before the first image's raise and 0xae after it, and the second image finds 0xae and writes nothing. Cycle 1 ON: CORE6 entry policy 8, status 0, PWCR 0x101; GPU clock pll=0xf9105300, about four reads per lock wait, one read per update bit; CORE6 status 8 before the ON deadline, misr_late=0x100. Cycle 1 OFF: CORE6 status 0 within the first poll and TOP5 status 0 within the owner's 10 ms, both with the GPU still clocked; PLL_GPU0 then reads 0x01105300 (bit 24 kept, control bits clear); the resource release passes; this is the first TOP5 transition from ON on a board. Cycle 2 ON: TOP5 goes from OFF to ON with the GPU clocked, the first TOP5 power-up handshake on a board; CORE6 entry policy 0, status 0, PWCR 0, which admission accepts as settled OFF; PLL_GPU0 locks directly at 1008 MHz; CORE6 reaches 8 after the policy write; snapshot 2 shows 0x07066008 = 8. The identity image prints GPU identity cycle=1 and cycle=2, each raw=0x240038006800b7 matches=1, and COMPLETE GPU power identity: 36.56.104.183 in two ON/OFF cycles, provider parked. Departures: cycle 1 OFF timing out at the CORE6 status poll (OFF step 1) means CORE6 does not complete OFF even while clocked, TOP5 and clocks stay on; TOP5 OFF failing or timing out (OFF step 2) means TOP5 does not complete OFF even while clocked, GPU stays clocked and CORE6 OFF per the snapshot; cycle 2 ON failing means the first OFF left the GPU in a state this ON order does not recover from, named by the error, step and snapshot. Two bringup changes altered structures that struct bb_power embeds (the counter clock's and the power service's), so the builder also compiles the board-bundle power service, its trace helpers, the counter clock and the PMIC native adapter; built against the checkpoint's power.c the client read every power-service field after the clock 8 bytes from where it is written, which the host checks caught at the first deadline check. A power service built before the branch verifies DCDC4 only at 800 mV, so the provider-readiness checkpoint 3adfa4ad... runs first on every port 3-1 lifetime; every other row is built from the branch and accepts either voltage; bundle 6 accepts either snapshot; NPU images on port 3-3 verify DCDC4 the same way but no GPU image runs there.
conclusion: First two runs (power-only-first, power-only-second) failed for the reasons in their records and were fixed; the full prediction, including cycle 2 ON, has no result record of its own. OFF is qualified through the firmware-stop image (docs/designs/gpu-firmware-stop.md).

hypothesis: The EL3 security setup, including write 11 (S_TZMA), runs through the kernel check and the refreeze sequence on port 3-3.
prediction: The EL3 qualification runbook (docs/board-runbooks/el3-qualification.md) runs in one fresh port 3-3 lifetime. It runs the kernel check with the security writes including S_TZMA (write 11), a read of six of the written words, and the six runs of the refreeze sequence on the refrozen native image 6fd7af86..., whose pre-scheduler overlay calls the native setup (set board-bundles-20261025-10/port-3-3/). Predictions: each run returns, both security switches read 7, the three S_TZMA words read 0, SPC 0x020540e0 reads 0xfffffbff, and every 91-word capture equals the clean capture. The NPU state read of 2026-10-25 read 21 words, none written by these writes; they should read the same values.
conclusion: Not yet run as a result record here; the runbook states the setup has run on a board once, in the vendor-state GPU image on port 3-1, without write 11 and only through the single-core monitor. See also docs/evidence/native-refreeze-1025.jsonl.

hypothesis: The SMC0 and wrapper drm_ctrl secure-configuration writes of the vendor start are safe to add to the firmware start.
prediction: The vendor RGXDoStart calls sunxi_secure_config before RGXStart: SMC0 0x0a0000b0 = 2, then wrapper drm_ctrl 0x01880014 = 0 (sunxi_platform.c:964-979); the SunstoneOS start lacked both (action 5 of the vendor action plan). RGXPostPowerState reads RGX_CR_TIMER (0x01800160) before RGXDoStart (rgxtimecorr.c:300), which the start lacked; the firmware state gave the firmware 400 MHz (A733_GPU_INITIAL_HZ) while the core runs at A733_GPU_CORE_HZ, 1008 MHz, which the firmware's timer correlation needs. Probe-read diagnostic on the default path (row 17): the identity, the two secure-configuration writes with read-backs, the identity again, and the restores. Prediction: both identities 36.56.104.183, SMC0 +0xb0 reads 2 and drm_ctrl 0 after the writes, both restored, and a return. A return with these values makes the secure configuration safe to add to the firmware start. Firmware start: the default ON, the secure configuration, the timer read and the 35-step start of pvr_gpu_start.c; prediction: the firmware-started byte at system-init offset 352 becomes 1 within the start deadline, followed by the firmware's first host-visible status in its shared structures; a timeout leaves the MIPS wrapper and reset registers to read through the host interface. The firmware license (LICENSE.powervr line 14) forbids reverse engineering, so the start is derived only from the open-source host driver (rgxstartstop.c, rgxinit.c, rgxtimecorr.c, rgx_sunxi/sunxi_platform.c at kernel 2ac08e8c7), its interface headers and container fields the host driver reads; probe-read diagnostic image ae2afba7..., wrapper-read a2d05627..., identity 01849e62..., power-only b163b8fc... (built at 22501205 after the rebase onto bringup 49bc00da; the first two frozen in board-bundles-20261025-9/port-3-1/).
conclusion: Superseded by docs/designs/gpu-firmware-start.md, which derives the complete vendor sequence; that document records the secure-configuration probe-read as passed on its own and the start as qualified on the board (port 3-1).
narrative: Prediction carried over from the design; the outcome is taken from gpu-firmware-start.md.

hypothesis: The default GPU power path costs the register writes, waits and EL3 accesses the design lists, and changes the identity of the images the design names.
prediction: Counts compare the controller before the default path (work/gpu-core6-c-1024 at 750fa092) with the default path. Before -> after: controller register writes per ON 11 -> 16 and per OFF 4 -> 8 (checks/a733-gpu-power.c write trace); controller callbacks per ON with one clock sample per us 82 -> 182; PMIC transactions before the first ON of a platform 0 -> 3 (DCDC4 snapshot, write with readback, consumer sample; drivers/gpu/a733_gpu_platform.c, checks/power-domains-service.c); before a later ON 0 -> 0; fixed waits per ON one 1 us settle -> two 20 us PLL waits, 1.2 ms once per platform for DCDC4; EL3 accesses per image start 0 -> 31 writes and 3 reads, 33 writes when an earlier image left DMA running (checks/a733-monitor-are.py, case are-37). The ON adds the 10 PLL_GPU0 writes of the enable and set-rate helpers, each read back, and removes the five CORE6 delay-row writes and their read-backs.

conclusion: Host models and an instruction check give the counts above; they are not a board result except where a record of a board run names them. Of 56 default images, 34 change; the 22 unchanged are a733-smp-diagnostic (until the commit after a071620a added the writes to platform/a733-smp/boot.c), kernel-check and the DMA, I2S stream and duplex, NPU service, radio and SMP models.
narrative: Image identity comparison: the central targets and the supervised and resident OS images were built at the branch base (750fa092) and at a071620a, each from a clean archive at the same path, and compared by SHA-256 and loadable bytes. Of 56 images, 34 change. Code changes through an EL3 entry's security writes (17): a733-cxx-check, a733-kernel-check, a733-memtest, a733-mimus, a733-mimus-usb, a733-power-probe, a733-storage-probe and a733-usb-runtime (the returning monitor); a733-smp-cached-diagnostic, a733-smp-observe, a733-smp-supervised, sunstone-a733-board, -camera, -hdmi, -mimus-native, -smp-cached-devices and -storage-maintenance (the SMP cached boot); the board, camera, HDMI, mimus-native and storage-maintenance images also link the changed PMIC provider, owner, consumer and resource manager. Code changes through the GPU and supply path (10): sunstone-a733-gpu-render (SMP cached boot, GPU controller, platform and supply); the supervised and resident OS images (SMP cached boot, PMIC provider, owner, consumer and resource manager; their default configuration links no GPU controller); npu-startup-model (PMIC provider, owner and resource manager); and the six GPU service models (gpu-compute-service-model, gpu-freelist-service-model, gpu-irq-model, gpu-memory-model, gpu-power-service-model, gpu-service-model), which link the changed GPU stand-in of checks/pvr-gpu-service.c and, for the power model, the controller. Debug information only (7): a733-cxx-model, a733-kernel-model, a733-mimus-model, a733-mimus-replay-model and a733-monitor-model build the monitor with MONITOR_QEMU, which compiles the writes out; i2s-file-model and i2s-runtime-model include a changed header; their loadable bytes are unchanged. The commit after a071620a adds the writes to platform/a733-smp/boot.c, so a733-smp-diagnostic also changes in code from there; the SMP models do not compile that file. Images built by application scripts change when rebuilt from this tree because they compile one of the EL3 entries: the four GPU diagnostic variants (at 22501205, after the rebase onto bringup 49bc00da: identity 01849e62..., power-only b163b8fc..., wrapper-read a2d05627..., probe-read ae2afba7...; the first two frozen in board-bundles-20261025-9/port-3-1/), and the returning USB, RTC, finite NPU and board-bundle images. Frozen evidence sets, including the provider-readiness checkpoint 3adfa4ad..., keep their images.
